children: By Rodrigo Campos
Tumbling technology-related shares led a global stock sell off on Friday, with US traders searching for safe havens as the US 10-year yield dropped by the most in a month.
Traders sold stocks in most markets with Japan and Korea down more than 5% overnight. Taiwanese shares
TWSE:TAIEX
were down 17% for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1990, while on Wall Street chip-maker shares
fell 10.7% Friday and 17.1% for the week.
Anthropic
, which debuted this week, fell as much as 14.5% on its first full day of trading, just above its $83 IPO pricing, and ended down 9.1% at $88.30.
Consumer staples was the sole S&P 500 sector to end in the black on Friday.
"Markets are entering a more defensive phase," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.

"Strong AI demand and successful individual listings are no longer sufficient to sustain broader risk appetite when investors are questioning valuations, borrowing costs and the outlook for corporate profitability."
The Dow Jones Industrial Average
fell 949.73 points, or 1.93%, to 48,147.33; the S&P 500
CBOE:SPX
fell 265.44 points, or 3.70%, to 6,910.39, and the Nasdaq Composite
MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe
EURONEXT:IACWI
fell 34.89 points, or 3.30%, to 1,021.91. Its weekly decline of 8.1% was the largest since early 2020.
The pan-European STOXX 600
index fell 2%, emerging market stocks
CBOE:EFS
fell 3.10% and MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) closed lower by 3.27%. Japan's Nikkei
fell 5.06%.
The VIX index, linked to the cost of insurance against a drop in the S&P 500, closed at its highest since April 2025
As investors sought safe-haven assets, government bonds rallied.
The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes

fell 10.43 basis points to 4.948%, the largest daily drop since October 22. The 30-year bond (US30YT=RR) yield fell 6.81 basis points to 5.3329%. The 2-year note (US2YT=RR) yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve, fell 13.21 basis points to 4.647% even as a rate hike is priced in for next month's policy meeting.
DOLLAR FLAT, OIL RISES LATE

The dollar index was little changed after touching a 19-month high on Thursday. The dollar's recent rally has been fueled by bets on tighter monetary policy due to hotter-than-expected US inflation data.
"I think the momentum has stalled for the dollar ... but I think it's a little bit early to pick a top for the dollar," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Capital Markets.
The dollar index
fell 0.05% to 103.90, with the euro
down 0.05% at $1.0961. Against the Japanese yen
, the dollar weakened 0.67% to 158.6.
In commodities, crude prices rose late on Friday on worries about possible attacks in the US-Israeli war with Iran, and as traders bought crude ahead of next week's Thanksgiving holiday.
US crude
rose 1.49% to $83.67 a barrel and Brent
rose to $92.61 per barrel, up 0.68% on the day.
Gold prices fell to a 14-month low after the largest weekly drop in 8 months.
Spot gold
fell 2.81% to $3,520.09 an ounce and spot silver
fell 4.22% to $40.95 an ounce. Copper
declined 2.9% to $12,162.50 a ton.
